solutionNote: Tyler's worked solution for Ollie. Every decision in the walkthrough is measured against it; Step 6 shows how close the student got.

params.label: Imported files
params.off: Some of the files are not the ones this case uses. Ollie is a small dog, so both interfaces come from the small pair.
params.note: Ollie's scan, the socket surface cut from it, and the small mechanical and solid interfaces.

params.label: Pelvic plane
params.off: Not the plane this case uses. It sits on the X maximum face of the attachment surface, looking back along -X.
params.note: X maximum, Y centroid, Z centroid, with the normal pointing back along -X.

params.label: Interface plane
params.off: Not the face the leg mount sits on. On the small solid interface it is the Z minimum face, with the normal along +Z.
params.note: X centroid, Y centroid, Z minimum, with the normal along +Z.

params.label: Interface position
params.off: The interface sits somewhere else on the body. Drag the position onto the surface, then fine-tune with the X, Y and Z adjustments in Step 2d.
params.note: Measured with the Step 2d X, Y and Z adjustments folded in, because that is where the interface actually ends up.

params.label: Lateral angle
params.low: Tilted further out than the solution, which pushes the leg away from under the body.
params.high: Tilted further in than the solution, which tucks the leg under the body.

params.label: Medial angle
params.low: Angled further toward the midline than the solution, so the leg crosses under the body.
params.high: Angled further away from the midline than the solution, so the paw splays outward.

params.label: Interface rotation
params.low: Turned further one way than the solution, so the paw points off the walking line.
params.high: Turned further the other way than the solution, so the paw points off the walking line.
params.note: -180 degrees, the interface turned right around.

params.label: Min lattice thickness
params.low: Thinner struts than the solution. Thin struts save weight but flex, and they can crack where the straps pull.
params.high: Thicker struts than the solution. Thick struts are stiff but heavy, and they trap heat against a small dog.

params.label: Max lattice thickness
params.low: A thinner maximum than the solution, so the load-bearing areas may not stiffen enough.
params.high: A thicker maximum than the solution, adding weight where the socket should stay light.

params.label: Spatial weighting
params.low: Less weighting toward the loaded areas than the solution, so thickness is spread more evenly.
params.high: More weighting toward the loaded areas than the solution, so the rest of the socket stays thin.

params.label: Lattice point density
params.low: A lower point density than the solution. Bigger openings are lighter and cooler, but the shell gets floppy.
params.high: A higher point density than the solution. A dense lattice is stiffer but heavier, and it traps more heat.

params.label: Attachment points
params.off: The screws do not land where this case puts them. There are six, in two rows of three along the body.
params.note: Six points: three along each side, spread front to back.
